title: Derivative of the mollification of a globally Lipschitz function: D(ρ⋆F)(x) = ∫ρ(y)·DF(x−y)dy (parent Step 7)
statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and L ≥ 0, and let F : ℝ^P → ℝ satisfy |F(a) − F(b)| ≤ L|a − b| for all a, b ∈ ℝ^P. Let ρ : ℝ^P → ℝ be continuous with compact support. Write DF(z) := fderiv ℝ F z for the Fréchet derivative, which is 0 where F is not differentiable. Then for every x ∈ ℝ^P, the function x′ ↦ ∫ ρ(y)F(x′ − y) dλ^P(y) is Fréchet differentiable at x. Its derivative is the Bochner integral ∫ ρ(y)·DF(x − y) dλ^P(y), an element of the space of continuous linear maps ℝ^P → ℝ. Here λ^P is Lebesgue measure (`volume` on `Eucl P`).
lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (F : Eucl P → ℝ) (L : ℝ≥0), LipschitzWith L F → ∀ ρ : Eucl P → ℝ, Continuous ρ → HasCompactSupport ρ → ∀ x : Eucl P, HasFDerivAt (fun x' : Eucl P => ∫ y, ρ y * F (x' - y)) (∫ y, ρ y • fderiv ℝ F (x - y)) x
